evidence.claim: Guided residual inversion is a reconstruction candidate distinct from adding unrelated random noise.
limitations: Captioned other-model experiments do not establish our SD1.5 empty-prompt profile.
assumptions: Published equations can be independently adapted with bounded numerical checks.

evidence.claim: GNRI is not uniformly highest-fidelity: Appendix H2 reports a slower stochastic alternative with higher PSNR.
limitations: Different timing and stochastic storage profile; not our experiment.

evidence.claim: The inspected SD1.5 table reports ReNoise+TRDI 22.67 dB and GNRI+TRDI 22.32 dB, below the proposal's 35 dB target.
limitations: Captioned 1000-pair sample and 50 steps; no numerical equivalence to local single-image result.

evidence.claim: Decoder adaptation targets repeated VAE reconstruction degradation; it is relevant if our codec control fails, not guaranteed single-pass success.
limitations: Inspected official repository provides no ready code/weights; iterative task differs.
assumptions: Measured codec controls will inform whether decoder work is justified.
User authorization changes reconstruction candidate flexibility only; exact compute and core claim boundaries remain separate.
open_questions: Does the existing VAE-only native output pass source targets?
Can empty-conditioned SD1.5 bounded inversion improve both reconstruction and keyed latent/DCT performance?
Which source-latent/decoder alternative passes actual rights, quality, safety and resource checks if codec loss dominates?
